subject: Clarify: What Redwood retains after a hosted demo (EU region)
messages:
From: Lena Fischer <lena@olivehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on what Redwood keeps after demo (EU)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — it was helpful. Before we spin up the pilot in our EU environment we have two concise questions the security team asked me to confirm:

1) For a hosted demo in the EU region, what is Redwood's default retention for: the original request (our prompt), the model output, and any transient streaming fragments?
2) If we ask for deletion or stop the demo, what is the deletion path (console vs. support ticket) and how quickly can you provide proof of deletion for our auditors?

A few background constraints: we will not enable any long-term indexing or embedding features in the pilot; the demo will include short health record snippets as examples (redacted).

Can you point me to a short matrix or runbook we can share with our security folks?

Best,
Lena
Security Manager, Olive Health


From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Fischer <lena@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps after demo (EU)

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear questions. I summarized the default behavior below and attached a compact retention matrix (retention-matrix.csv) for your security team. TL;DR: hosted EU defaults are conservative, with short troubleshooting windows and an expedited erasure path.

Quoted for context:
> For a hosted demo in the EU region, what is Redwood's default retention for: the original request (our prompt), the model output, and any transient streaming fragments?
> If we ask for deletion or stop the demo, what is the deletion path (console vs. support ticket) and how quickly can you provide proof of deletion for our auditors?

Answers (default hosted EU behavior unless you request a custom contract):

- Prompts / original requests: retained in encrypted request logs for 30 days by default. These logs are used only for debugging, replaying issues, and quality regressions. They are not used to train models.

- Model outputs / responses: treated as "derived artifacts" — by default they are retained for 30 days if generated during an interactive/hosted session. If you turn on "persist_outputs" (an opt-in setting for customers), outputs are retained longer and can be exported to customer storage; otherwise outputs are purged from persistent storage after the 30-day window and removed from indexables.

- Streaming fragments (partial tokens/chunks sent over a stream): not written to durable storage by default. Streaming buffers are captured in transient telemetry for up to 24 hours to help diagnose failed sessions (e.g., to correlate incomplete streams). That telemetry is rotated and purged automatically; it is not included in exported logs unless explicitly requested when troubleshooting.

- KV cache and GPU-resident state: never persisted to disk as part of our hosted offering; cache entries are in-memory and are flushed on session termination (typically within seconds).

- Attachments referenced in the conversation: attachments you upload during a session are stored according to the attachment type — in your case small files used for the demo will be stored in the EU region and will follow the same 30-day retention unless you request immediate removal.

Deletion / erasure workflow:

1) Self-serve removals: for objects that were created as explicit exports (persisted outputs, embeddings exported to your S3), you can remove them via the Redwood Console immediately.
2) Support removal: for server-side request logs and streaming telemetry (the troubleshooting artifacts retained inside Redwood), please open a support ticket (support@redwood.ai) with the thread id + timestamp range. We process erasure requests for hosted accounts in the EU within 3 business days for the majority of requests.
3) Audit evidence: after support completes deletion, we provide a signed deletion report that includes which storage buckets/keys were cleared and timestamps. Typical turnaround for proof of deletion is 5 business days from ticket close.

Examples (short scenarios to share with auditors):
- Scenario A - Interactive demo (no persist_outputs): requests & outputs — 30 days retention; streaming fragments — transient up to 24 hours; erasure via support ticket, proof in 5 business days.
- Scenario B - Demo with "persist_outputs" ON: outputs exported to your S3 — immediate console delete available; Redwood will retain minimal metadata for billing/traceability for 90 days unless contract says otherwise.

What I attached: retention-matrix.csv (simple rows for Request / Output / Streaming / Attachments and actions & TTL). Also looping in Marissa (cc) for the SOC2/evidence specifics if Olive needs formal artifacts.

If you'd like, we can also run a short pilot run where we show you the Console removal flow and then generate a deletion report while on the call. That usually satisfies auditor questions quickly.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Neha — this is helpful, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups from our security reviewer:

1) When you say "minimal metadata for billing/traceability" for exported outputs, can you list the exact fields kept (example: timestamp, user-id, job-id, hash)? We need to know what persists after console deletion for 90 days.
2) For the 30-day request/response retention window, is there any scenario where those logs are retained longer (e.g., legal hold, active incident investigations)? If so, how will Olive be notified and how is access gated?

Also, Marissa — could you confirm what the SOC2 report snapshot contains vs. the signed deletion report Neha mentioned?

Thanks,
Lena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Fischer <lena@olivehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 16:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps after demo (EU)

Hi Lena — quick legal + compliance confirm:

- Metadata retained after console deletion (90-day billing traceability): we keep a minimal record set for invoicing and operational traceability. Fields: event_timestamp, account_id (hashed customer id), request_hash (SHA-256 of the request payload), action_type (generate/stream/export), and job_id. We do NOT keep full prompt text or PII in those billing trace entries. Those records are encrypted and stored in the EU region.

- Exceptions to retention windows: logs may be retained beyond the default windows for two narrow reasons: (1) legal hold (court order/subpoena) or (2) active security incident investigation initiated by Redwood or coordinated with the customer. In either case we notify the primary account contact and the customer's security contact within 48 hours of the hold and provide the minimal scope and justification. Access is strictly role-based and logged; only the compliance team and a scoped set of SREs have access and all access is audited.

- SOC2 snapshot vs deletion report: the SOC2-Summary.pdf I've attached is our standard summary (controls mapped to data handling and retention). The signed deletion report Neha referenced is generated per erasure request and contains the exact keys/buckets cleared and time stamps with a compliance officer signature. SOC2 is a controls attestation (annual/quarterly), while the deletion report is transaction-level evidence for a specific erasure action (generated on request).

If Olive would like, we can add a short paragraph to the deletion report confirming that no PII remains in the deleted artifacts; we include that language routinely for healthcare pilots.

I'll leave operational details to Neha to coordinate, but happy to jump on a call if you want a triage runbook walk-through.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Trust, Redwood Inference
